validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: SUMED (Suez-Mediterranean Pipeline) is one of the best-documented crude oil pipelines in the world — a strategic Suez Canal bypass built after the 1967 canal closure. Confirmed independently by: Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumed_pipeline), the operator's own site (sumed.org), the U.S. EIA (eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=61025), and current 2026 reporting (Egypt Independent, 'Egypt's SUMED oil flows jump 150% on Red Sea trade rerouting') confirming it is actively operating today amid Red Sea shipping disruptions. Correctly classified Fuel=Oil (crude oil transshipment line, not gas/products). No hallucination risk here — this is a Tier-1 real, active, well-known asset.

validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE WATCHLIST RESOLVED: P0530 and P5121 both read 'Sumed Oil Pipeline', Ain Sukhna->Alexandria, 320 km / 42 in / 1,250,000 bpd — identical on every visible spec. This is NOT a duplicate/relabel. Multiple independent sources (Wikipedia, sumed.org's own facilities page) confirm SUMED is physically built as TWO PARALLEL 42-inch, 320 km pipelines sharing one corridor (Ain Sukhna -> Dahshour booster -> Sidi Kerir), with a combined system capacity of 2.5 million bpd. GEM has deliberately modeled this as two rows via segment_name — P0530 = 'Pipeline 1', P5121 = 'Pipeline 2' — which is the correct way to represent a genuine twin-line system, not a double-count. Minor cross-row inconsistency worth a separate note (not this row's defect): sumed.org's own history page dates the FIRST line's start to January 1977 (first tanker loaded at Sidi Kerir) and the SECOND line/phase to October 1978 (capacity doubled to 80 million tons/yr) — P0530's StartYear1=1977 matches 'Pipeline 1' correctly, but P5121 ('Pipeline 2') also carries StartYear1=1977 in the worklist, which per sumed.org's own timeline should likely be 1978. That is P5121's issue to flag/fix, not this row's.

validity.researcher_notes: GEOGRAPHY ERROR: sheet has StartLocation='Ain Sukhna terminal', StartPrefecture/District='Sinai Peninsula', StartState/Province='North Red Sea'. Ain Sukhna (Ain Sokhna) is on the WESTERN/African shore of the Gulf of Suez, in Suez Governorate — roughly 55 km south of Suez city and ~120 km east of Cairo. It is NOT part of the Sinai Peninsula, which lies on the opposite (eastern) side of the Suez Canal/Gulf of Suez. Confirmed via multiple independent sources describing Ain Sokhna as a town in Suez Governorate on the Gulf of Suez's west bank. This is also an internal-consistency defect: four OTHER Egypt-oil rows in this same tracker that reference the identical Ain Sokhna location (P7331 EndPrefecture/District, P7315 EndPrefecture/District, P7327 StartPrefecture/District, P7321 StartLocation) all correctly write 'Ain Sokhna' — only P0530 and its twin P5121 substitute the wrong 'Sinai Peninsula'. Separately, the sheet's StartState/Province taxonomy for this location is itself inconsistent tracker-wide (variously 'Suez', 'Suez Gulf', 'North Red Sea' across different Ain Sokhna rows) — flagging as a broader open question for Update, not resolving it here since no single value is clearly the sheet's intended standard.

validity.researcher_notes: LIKELY MISATTRIBUTION: FuelSource='Gulf of Suez' appears to conflate the GEOGRAPHIC LOCATION of the intake terminal (Ain Sukhna sits on the Gulf of Suez) with the ACTUAL SOURCE of the crude oil moving through the line. Per gem_schema.md's own convention (documented for the gas sheet but applied identically across every other Egypt-oil FuelSource cell in this worklist), FuelSource should name the specific upstream field/terminal feeding the line, not a generic body of water. SUMED carries NO locally-produced Gulf-of-Suez crude at all — it is a pure transshipment line: VLCCs deliver imported crude to Ain Sukhna, which is then pumped to Sidi Kerir for reloading onto tankers bound for the Mediterranean/Europe. Al Jazeera (2020, still describing the same unchanged system): 'The vast majority of crude entering the pipeline comes from Saudi Arabia, with Kuwait and Iraq contributing much less' and 'designed to pump 2.5 million barrels of Persian Gulf crude'. Wikipedia independently corroborates: SUMED provides 'an alternative to the Suez Canal for transporting oil from the Persian Gulf region to the Mediterranean.' Two independent sources agree the origin is Persian/Arabian Gulf crude (predominantly Saudi), not Gulf-of-Suez production — the current value is not merely imprecise, it names the wrong body of water for the wrong reason (intake geography vs. crude origin).

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC CHECK: Length=320 km and Diameter=42 in both confirmed at high tier by 3 independent sources (Wikipedia, operator sumed.org's own facilities page, and multiple current news sources) — no disagreement found anywhere. Status=operating confirmed current as of 2026 (Egypt Independent: 'SUMED oil flows jump 150% on Red Sea trade rerouting', describing live 2026 throughput). ProposalYear=1974 matches sumed.org's own history: 'SUMED was established by Law No 7, 1974' (precursor five-nation agreement was Dec 1973 per a 1973 NYT piece in the wiki's own citation list, so 1974 = formal legal establishment, a defensible ProposalYear anchor). StartYear1=1977 matches sumed.org's own timeline precisely for THIS line ('Pipeline 1'): first tanker (Esthel) loaded at Sidi Kerir January 1977. CAVEAT on Capacity=1,250,000 bpd: no source states a per-line figure explicitly — every source (Wikipedia, EIA, Al Jazeera) states only the combined SYSTEM capacity of 2.5 million bpd across both twin lines. 1,250,000 x 2 = 2,500,000 is an exact, arithmetically consistent split for two identically-specced (42in/320km) parallel lines, but it is a derived value, not a directly cited one — tier medium for Capacity specifically, high for everything else in this cluster.

fills.researcher_notes: SUMED is a crude oil transshipment pipeline; both sources describe it as such.
Actively operating and carrying record/near-record throughput as of 2026 per current Egyptian press coverage; EIA background confirms the standing 2.5M bpd design capacity.

Operator's own history page: 'SUMED was established by Law No 7, 1974' (January 1974). Single strong primary source (medium tier) — the earlier Dec-1973 five-nation political agreement reported by the NYT is a precursor negotiation, not the same event, so not counted as a second independent corroboration of the 1974 date specifically.
Operator's own timeline: first tanker loaded at Sidi Kerir January 1977, marking commissioning of this (the first) line. Wikipedia independently states the system was commissioned 1977.

Neither source states a per-line figure — both state the combined 2-line system capacity as 2.5 million bpd. 1,250,000 bpd is an exact half-split across two identically-specced (42in/320km) parallel lines, which is arithmetically sound but not a directly cited per-line number, hence medium tier rather than high. Cited refs support the combined total that the per-line figure derives from.
